claim: Morgan's canon is a rule of thumb for lowering over-interpretation, not Occam's razor (Mikhalevich et al. 2017; Heyes 2012): a simpler explanation does not mean a simpler mechanism, and Starzak (2016) and Heyes (2012) argue that nothing independently justifies preferring explanations lower on the scale.
agent_test: Compare a G3 that forces 'name the simplest rival and a discriminating test' against one that forces 'pick the simplest', at equal tokens, on contamination-sensitive items; expect the first to lose less.
audit_note: The last clause is stated as settled fact but is a philosophical position (Starzak 2016, Heyes 2012 on Morgan's failure to justify the canon), not an established finding; a01 and b01/a13 duplicate sources (Mercado commentary listed twice).
claim_before_audit: Morgan's canon is a rule of thumb for lowering over-interpretation, not Occam's razor: a simpler explanation does not mean a simpler mechanism, and nothing independently justifies preferring explanations lower on the scale.

claim: Pfungst's Clever Hans control worked by varying one thing (can the questioner be seen, does the questioner know): 50/56 correct (89%) when Hans saw the questioner versus 2/35 (6%) when not. The reusable method is a differential test that removes the suspected cue channel. Verified in Pfungst's own text: 102 blinder tests, 35 not seen (2 correct, 6%), 56 seen (89%), 11 undecided (18%).
agent_test: For each solved item, run a cue-ablated twin (surface cue removed, logic kept) and require the answer to survive.
audit_note: Minor: Pfungst reports 89% (about 50 of 56), so 50/56 is back-computed; Samhita and Gross confirm the method but give no percentages.

claim: Dog-pointing owner-cue test: dogs stayed above chance with a blindfolded, enhancing or decreasing owner (N=17-18 per group, p=.002-.003) and were at chance with no pointing, so the owner-cue explanation did not account for the effect.
agent_test: Not agent-specific; example that a cue explanation can be tested and rejected, not assumed.

claim: A low-level rival explanation gives mixed results under direct test: the inanimate-control replication of ape anticipatory looking had 22/43 (51%) looking versus 22/30 (73%) in the original, with first looks 14/22 to target (p=.28). The effect is weaker than the original, not cleanly refuted.
agent_test: Treat a weakened-but-not-null effect under control as 'partly cue-driven'; score items on a graded scale, not pass/fail.

claim: Implicit anticipatory-looking false-belief effects are inconsistent in humans: a two-lab preregistered replication of Southgate et al. (2007) found 49/90 infants (54%) anticipated at familiarisation and 22/49 at test (p=.57), and a three-experiment study (Kulke et al. 2019) found mixed results, with first saccades at chance in some conditions (e.g. 7/12 in FB1, BF10 0.64) and no unambiguous evidence for reliable spontaneous ToM.
agent_test: Require a pass to hold across repeated independent runs and rephrasings before counting it; track single-run pass versus repeat-pass rate.
audit_note: Kulke and Rakoczy found a mixed pattern (some conditions replicate, e.g. belief-congruent looking significant in some FB conditions; 7/12 is one condition, FB1, in adult Study 1), not first saccades at chance across the study; one failed replication plus a mixed-results study does not show poor replication in general.
claim_before_audit: Implicit anticipatory-looking false-belief effects replicate poorly in humans: 49/90 infants (54%) anticipated at familiarisation and 22/49 at test (p=.57) in a two-lab preregistered replication; a three-experiment study found first saccades at chance (e.g. 7/12, BF10 0.64).

claim: Headline LLM theory-of-mind success is fragile under logic-preserving perturbation: GPT-3.5 passes the original unexpected-contents task (99% chocolate) but gives the same wrong answer on variants (transparent bag 95%, cannot read 98%, trusted friend 97%).
agent_test: Build 5 mutated twins per benchmark item (same logic, changed surface or perceptual access); report pass-on-original versus pass-on-all-twins for plain and scaffold arms.

claim: Stress tests show shortcut behaviour: GPT-3.5 gets 81% overall on ToMi but 46% on false-belief questions (near chance); GPT-4 gets 27% on FauxPas-EAI, below the most-frequent-class baseline; adversarial variants collapse performance.
agent_test: Always report subset scores next to totals; alarm when the critical subset is far below the overall score.

claim: Counterfactual and perturbation tests show surface-statistics dependence across independent groups: GPT-4 cipher 51% vs 13% by output probability (Embers); default vs counterfactual gap (Wu et al.); GSM-NoOp drops up to 65% (Mirzadeh et al.); fresh GSM1k drops up to 8% for some families, Spearman r2=0.36 against GSM8k generation likelihood (Zhang et al.).
agent_test: Run each task in default and rare/counterfactual form; the scaffold counts as helping only if it shrinks the default-minus-counterfactual gap at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: Zhang et al. frame GSM1k gaps as contamination/overfitting, and Wu et al. appears three times in the evidence (one paper).

claim: Test-time scaffolds do not reliably close the perturbation gap: chain-of-thought left SimpleToM behaviour judgement under 40% for most models, 0-16 shots narrow but do not remove Wu's gap, and CoT is unfaithful to biasing features (Turpin, drops up to 36%). Exception: a reminder prompt lifted one model from 24.9% to 84.1% but others far less. Reasoning models (o1, o3-mini, GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1) narrow but do not remove the SimpleToM explicit-versus-applied gap: behaviour judgment 32.5 to 65.8 against mental-state accuracy of 85 to 99.
agent_test: Test a 'consider the other agent's state' reminder operator versus plain CoT at equal tokens, per model, and report variance across models.
audit_note: Minor: b21, b22, d06, d07 are all the same SimpleToM paper (one source); reminder lifted Claude-3.5-Sonnet judgement 24.9 to 84.1 as stated.

claim: Consistency across question forms exposes illusory competence: FANToM strictest score is 87.5 for humans and 26.6 (or 14.8 in a later run) for GPT-4 with CoT, though single questions look fine.
agent_test: Score an answer only if the same fact is answered consistently under 3 reformulations; compare to single-form accuracy.

claim: Positive controls guard against a trivial strategy: adding true-belief controls dropped davinci-003 from 90% to 20% on false-belief tasks, so earlier scores reflected a shortcut.
agent_test: Pair every test item with a control whose correct answer is the opposite; count a pass only if both are correct.

claim: Failure can be task demand, not missing ability: rewording faux pas to a likelihood question lifted GPT-4 to or above human level; small-model demand gaps shrink with size. A failure in one format does not prove a simple mechanism. Hu and Frank find the demand gap in four domains (significant size-by-method interaction in three), but did not test chain of thought.
agent_test: For any failing item, rerun in a lower-demand format (likelihood, forced choice) before concluding the capability is missing.

claim: Human comparison is mixed: GPT-4 beats humans on irony and hinting (both reported P=.040) but is below on faux pas (P=5.4e-5), with about 50 humans per test. Aggregate 'passes ToM' claims hide this.
agent_test: None directly; warning on aggregate claims.

claim: Contamination can be detected without training data, but the two methods differ in API use: guided-prompt completion matched human labels 92-100% (best variant 14/14 and 13/14 partitions) with 10 instances per split and plain text calls, while the exchangeability-order test needs prompt log probabilities, detects 1,000-item sets in a 1.4B model only from about 4 or more duplicates, and misses single exposures.
agent_test: Run a guided continuation-from-prefix check on visible items (about 10 prompts plus a match judge per partition). Use the order test only where prompt log probabilities exist.
audit_note: Minor: Oren et al. say detection threshold is around 4 duplicates but abstract also says sometimes detected at only 2 copies.

claim: Researchers endorse the canon unevenly: 70.5% of 210 respondents (of 1,001 invited) call it important and 39.7% sometimes hope for a result; a 2025 survey finds they use it as parsimony, not as an associative-versus-cognitive rule.
agent_test: None; background on how the rule is used.

claim: Neither pole is a default: association-blindness and simple-mindedness (Heyes 2012) are both errors, and anthropomorphism is the error Morgan's canon guards against, so a simple and a rich rival should each be listed with a discriminating test (Heyes' ghost control, Penn and Povinelli's multi-condition competitive protocol) rather than one assumed.
agent_test: Compare an operator that must generate one cheap-mechanism rival and one rich-mechanism rival plus a discriminating probe against a no-rival baseline, equal tokens.
audit_note: Heyes names association-blindness and simple-mindedness as the two errors, not anthropomorphism; anthropomorphism as an error comes from Morgan's tradition and other sources, not from Heyes or Pang et al. Ghost control and nine-condition design are confirmed.
claim_before_audit: Neither pole is a default: anthropomorphism and association-blindness are both errors, so a simple and a rich rival should each be listed with a discriminating test (ghost control, nine-condition design) rather than one assumed.

claim: No published LLM agent loop was found that uses Morgan's canon or an explicit simpler-explanation rule as an operator; closest practices are perturbation twins, consistency checks and contamination tests. Nearest tested operator, a forced generic self-review, lowered accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1).
agent_test: Open build; see K16 and K08 tests.

claim: Once a perturbation generator or benchmark is published it can be trained on, so a later pass proves less.
agent_test: Keep a held-back private mutation generator; compare scores on public versus fresh mutations.

claim: A forced review step without outside feedback can lower accuracy. GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA fell from 75.8 to 38.1 after one self-correction round and GPT-4 GSM8K from 95.5 to 89.0 after two, while oracle-label versions looked strong. A rival-plus-probe operator therefore needs a keep-the-answer exit and an equal-call comparison with plain chain of thought before it is trusted.
agent_test: Run plain CoT, CoT plus generic recheck, and CoT plus named-rival-plus-probe at equal tokens; report right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right flips separately.

claim: The applied-versus-explicit theory-of-mind gap persists in 2025-26 reasoning models. SimpleToM mental-state accuracy is 85-99% but behaviour judgment is 32.5% (o1), 40.0% (GPT-5), 41.3% (o3-mini), 59.5% (o1-preview) and 65.8% (DeepSeek-R1). Ullman-style and FANToM-style twins on these models were not found.
agent_test: Score the same fact at three levels (state, prediction, judgment) and count an item as passed only if all three agree.

claim: Meaning-preserving prompt changes move scores widely: up to 76 accuracy points across formats for LLaMA-2-13B, up to 56 (median 6.4) for GPT-3.5, and model rankings change across instruction paraphrases (Kendall W about .27 to .78 over 6.5M instances). A single pass on one wording is not a trustworthy score. No study gives a stopping number of rephrasings.
agent_test: Report mean and worst case over at least about ten paraphrases or formats per task and keep the spread, not one score.
audit_note: Minor: Kendall W upper value is .787 (about .79); 'no study gives a stopping number' is an absence claim not verifiable from sources.

claim: Paraphrase and translation hide test items from n-gram and embedding decontamination: a 13B model trained on rephrased MMLU items reached 85.9 while undetectable by n-gram overlap. Performance-based detection (ConStat) works on black boxes but needs reference models, and a rephrase gap can also come from training style (Phi models, GSM8k effect above 15%). The per-token ranking of paraphrase, name, number and format checks is untested.
agent_test: Start with paraphrase as the first cue ablation; compare gaps against a same-skill reference model before calling a gap contamination.
audit_note: Minor: ConStat attributes Phi GSM8k gap to reasoning-focused training as a suspicion; claim states 'can also come from training style' which is consistent.

claim: Original-source numbers checked: Pfungst's text and the Farrar 2021 survey match the secondary reports (see K02, K15). Krupenye 2016 (22/30) and Hare 2001 counts could not be verified because only abstracts were reachable.
agent_test: None; source hygiene. Quote Krupenye counts only with the Kano 2017 attribution.
